summary: Selective Monday scan of arXiv new listings after the weekend release gap. The strongest themes are chemically non-equilibrated QGP modeling, Beam Energy Scan cumulant backgrounds, strangeness system-size systematics, thermal spectral broadening in hadron feed-down, detector-level Bayesian inverse problems, and validation-first AI interfaces for HEP software.
strongest_paper: arXiv:2608.27687 is the strongest heavy-ion selection because it treats light and strange chemical non-equilibrium inside a full multistage Bayesian heavy-ion framework; arXiv:2608.27683 is the strongest AI/ML use case because it performs detector-level Bayesian amplitude inference with posterior coverage and transfer checks.
candidate_pool_note: Screened Monday 2026-08-31 arXiv new listings and relevant recent/replacement entries in nucl-th, nucl-ex, hep-ph, hep-ex, physics.data-an, stat.ML, and cs.LG. Selection was abstract-first, below the 50-paper ceiling, with deeper checks for papers retained in the report.

papers.title: Constraining Light and Strange Flavor Equilibration in Relativistic Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.abstract: Develops a dynamical light/strange quark fugacity framework coupled to hydrodynamics, particlization, hadronic transport, and Bayesian inference from RHIC Au+Au data.

papers.title: Hadronic rescattering effects on net-proton cumulants from functional renormalization group calculations
papers.abstract: Builds event-by-event proton distributions from fRG cumulants via maximum entropy and propagates them through SMASH to quantify hadronic-cascade modifications to BES net-proton cumulants.

papers.title: The role of strangeness and baryon enhancement in heavy-quark hadronisation from pp to Pb-Pb collisions with ALICE
papers.abstract: SQM2026 proceedings summary of ALICE charm-baryon and charm-meson ratios and nuclear modification measurements across pp and Pb-Pb systems.

papers.title: System-size dependence of strangeness production from p+p to Pb+Pb: quantitative tests of the K+/pi+ horn
papers.abstract: Compares transport, core-corona, canonical suppression, and SMES descriptions against NA61/SHINE, NA49, and STAR strangeness data across system sizes.

papers.title: Effect of Thermal Broadening on Light Hadron Production in Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.abstract: Extends FastReso to finite-width in-medium spectral functions and studies rho/omega broadening effects on pion, kaon, and proton spectra in LHC heavy-ion data.

papers.title: Color screening versus thermal decay as the mechanism of Upsilon suppression in high energy nuclear collisions
papers.abstract: Compares color-screening and thermal-decay suppression mechanisms for Upsilon production at RHIC using transport calculations and RAA data.

papers.title: Direct Bayesian Inference of Helicity Amplitudes from Detector-Level Scattering Data
papers.abstract: Uses a score-based diffusion posterior model trained on a forward simulator to infer helicity-amplitude parameters directly from detector-level measurements.

papers.title: HEPToolBench 1.2: Testing How Reliably Language Models Can Drive Particle Physics Software
papers.abstract: Benchmarks 42 language-model deployments on collider-simulation tasks and shows typed schema-mediated outputs strongly outperform raw native HEP-tool syntax generation.

papers.title: HEPLocalAgent 1.0: Running Collider Simulations from Plain-Language Requests on Your Own Computer
papers.abstract: Builds bounded collider simulation workflows from natural language via typed LLM proposals and deterministic validation for MadGraph, Pythia8, Delphes, and restricted MadAnalysis plans.

papers.title: Vertex reconstruction for a search for neutron-antineutron conversions with HIBEAM
papers.abstract: Compares deterministic and graph-neural-network TPC vertex reconstruction methods for HIBEAM/NNBAR neutron-antineutron conversion searches.

papers.title: Localizing Global Discrepancies: Marginal Contributions and Contextual Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Develops observation-level localization for global discrepancy statistics and applies efficient MMD-based estimators to LHC Olympics anomaly detection.

papers.title: How Architecture and Training Affect TPC Representations Across Experiments
papers.abstract: Uses frozen probes and random-weight controls to separate architecture-induced structure from learned transfer in TPC representations across GADGET II and AT-TPC tasks.

cautions.title: Quarkonium mechanism separation claims in arXiv:2608.28277
